method_details: H = valid Hoeffding bound. B = deterministic Bernstein bound with a variance upper bound. Centered DR uses fixed qhat=0.5, not a trained or oracle reward model. Tabular H uses conditional Hoeffding plus context-distribution uncertainty. Robust variants subtract exact reward-edit corrections; no additional clean reward data are supplied.
attack: For each defender, search candidates in increasing true value; maximize their winning margin by mixed-integer optimization. Also solve whether fallback can be forced. Pick the worst realized feasible outcome. Record unresolved ties/gaps. Binary flips only in the exact optimization; add feasible fractional attacks as a separate stress test.
attacker_knowledge: All logged records, logger, candidates, full defender and simulator true values (oracle attack).
cap: Declared cap equals actual cap in the main experiment.
primary_comparison: diverse_matched_gain, eta=0.05, epsilon=0.005; compare corrected centered DR with corrected IPS, nominal centered DR, nominal IPS and retain-baseline. Report every method and every grid cell, regardless of result.
success_criterion: In the primary cell, corrected centered DR must have a one-sided 95% harm upper bound below 5%, a 95% lower confidence bound on mean worst-attacked true improvement above +1 percentage point, and at least +1 pp paired improvement over corrected IPS. Empirical Pareto dominance requires no higher observed harm and no lower mean utility, with at least one strict inequality; statistical uncertainty is reported separately.
falsification: No retained useful improvement after stronger attacks, unresolved attack optimization, or domination by tabular/ordinary methods undermines the proposed contribution. A finite comparator set cannot establish global Pareto-optimality. Failure is retained and triggers narrowing or a topic-switch recommendation.
disclosure: The new environment deliberately tests separately useful policy alternatives while matching the original best value of +4 pp. It is a second hypothesis-driven experiment, not a replacement of the failed first experiment. No real-data or publication-novelty claim.
